result_text:
Per-extension entries are now named by the bare lower-cased extension (`java`, `js`, `xml`), and the metric ids are unchanged. The two affected test classes pass (`CodeConfigurationTest` 4/4, `NamedSourceCodeAspectTest` 6/6). I didn't run the full codeanalyzer suite or the reports module tests, and I didn't commit.

What changed:

- **`SourceCodeAspectUtils.java`**: `getAspectsPerExtensions` names each entry `extension` instead of `"  *." + extension`.
- **`AnalysisUtils.java`**: the `_EXT_` metric ids use the bare name directly, so `LINES_OF_CODE_MAIN_EXT_JAVA` and `NUMBER_OF_FILES_MAIN_EXT_JAVA` are unchanged. The textual summary line still prints as `  *.java: N files, …`, so it looks as before.
- **`LandscapeAnalysisResults.java`**: a new `getExtension` helper trims, strips a leading `*.` and lower-cases, so both `"  *.java"` (legacy) and `"java"` (new) map to `java`. It is applied in the per-extension lines-of-code aggregation and in `merge()`, which covers the main scope and the merged build/generated/other category. Per-repository breakdowns are built per entry, so a merged entry still lists every contributing repository.
- **`CodeConfigurationTest.java`** and **`NamedSourceCodeAspectTest.java`**: assertions updated from the decorated names to the bare ones.

Not changed: the reports module still has `.replace("*.", "")` calls. They are now no-ops on the new names and still handle legacy data, but they are outside the five files you listed, so I left them alone.
